_readme: Railway tools for ZeroScript, including a WORKING browserless login.
`railway login --browserless` prints a pairing code then BLOCKS until you
confirm in a browser. Called directly by a tool it hangs or is killed with
no output - that is the empty output you saw. railway-login.sh runs it in
the background, captures the pairing code, prints it and returns. You then
confirm in a browser and call railway_login_status.
Nothing here bypasses the browser step - that is not possible, and any tool
claiming otherwise would need your password. It only stops the blocking
For CI or an always-on deploy, skip login entirely: set RAILWAY_TOKEN
(project) or RAILWAY_API_TOKEN (account) in the environment before starting
the bridge, and the CLI authenticates with no prompt. Put it in the
environment - never paste a token into a chat.
Every 'run' is an argv LIST executed WITHOUT a shell, so an argument cannot
start a second command. There is no generic 'shell' tool by design.

target.name: Railway
target.offline_hint: Install the Railway CLI (npm i -g @railway/cli), then restart the bridge.

tools.name: railway_login
tools.description: Begin a Railway login. Returns a pairing code and URL for the user to open in a browser; it does NOT wait. After the user confirms, call railway_login_status.

tools.name: railway_login_status
tools.description: Check whether the Railway login has completed. Reports the account name only, never a token.

tools.name: railway_whoami
tools.description: Show which Railway account is currently authenticated.

tools.name: railway_status
tools.description: Show the linked Railway project and its services.

tools.name: railway_list
tools.description: List the Railway projects on this account.

tools.name: railway_logs
tools.description: Show recent deployment logs for the linked service.

tools.name: railway_variables
tools.description: List the environment variables of the linked service. Values are shown, so avoid this if secrets are set.

tools.name: railway_up
tools.description: Deploy the current workspace folder to Railway. Confirm with the user before using this.
